standard_prerequisites.name: Degree of an invertible sheaf on a proper curve and its behaviour under components, modification and tensor product
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Varieties, labels varieties-definition-degree-invertible-sheaf (statement, proof line 8107), varieties-lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components (proof line 8117), varieties-lemma-degree-birational-pullback (proof line 8131), varieties-lemma-degree-additive (proof line 8135), varieties-lemma-degree-tensor-product (proof line 8150), varieties-lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor (proof line 8155) and varieties-lemma-dim-1-proper-projective (proof line 8148)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the notion of degree being compared, its decomposition over the irreducible components of X, its invariance under a birational modification, its additivity in a filtration and in tensor products, and projectivity of a proper curve; none of them contains the comparison with c_1 itself.

standard_prerequisites.name: Filtering a finite locally free sheaf on a curve by invertible quotients after a modification
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, labels divisors-lemma-filter-after-modification (proof line 8122) and divisors-lemma-quasi-projective-Noetherian-pic-effective-Cartier (proof line 8143)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the modification X' -> X over which f^*E has a filtration with invertible successive quotients, and expresses an invertible sheaf on a proper curve as O(D) tensor O(D')^{-1} for effective Cartier divisors.

standard_prerequisites.name: Compatibility of first Chern classes with pushforward, additivity and the geometric case
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-pushforward-cap-cj (proof line 8126), lemma-additivity-chern-classes (proof line 8136), lemma-c1-cap-additive and lemma-chern-classes-E-tensor-L (proof line 8152) and lemma-geometric-cap (proof line 8157); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-pushdown-module (proof line 8172)
standard_prerequisites.use: Moves the computation across the modification, splits it additively over the filtration, reduces the invertible case to O(D), identifies c_1(O(D)) cap [X] with [D]_0, and converts the resulting sum of residue degrees into the dimension of the space of global sections of O_D.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case of a proper curve: write [X]_1 as the sum of the components with multiplicities, observe that c_1(E) cap [X]_1 is the corresponding sum of pushforwards of c_1(E|_{C_i}) cap [C_i], and use the analogous decomposition of the degree to reduce to X a proper curve over k (proof lines 8110-8118).

Kill the rank by a modification and additivity: choose f : X' -> X such that f^*E has a filtration with invertible successive quotients, use f_*[X']_1 = [X]_1 together with the pushforward formula for c_1 to compare the two degrees, and then use additivity of degree and of first Chern classes to reduce to E invertible (proof lines 8120-8137).

Settle the invertible case: write E as O(D) tensor O(D')^{-1} for effective Cartier divisors and reduce by additivity to E = O(D); the left hand side is deg(D) and the right hand side is deg([D]_0), and since [D]_0 is the sum over the points of D of length times the class of the point, the sum of the residue degrees equals dim_k Gamma(D, O_D) = deg(D) by the pushdown formula, using that D is affine (proof lines 8139-8173).
proof_roadmap: Split over the irreducible components and reduce to a proper curve (proof lines 8110-8118).
Apply a modification that turns E into a successive extension of invertible sheaves, then use additivity to reach rank one (proof lines 8120-8137).
For an invertible sheaf write it as a difference of two effective divisors and compare deg(D) with dim_k Gamma(D, O_D) (proof lines 8139-8173).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the degree of a finite locally free module of constant rank on a proper curve over a field with the degree of its first Chern class capped with the fundamental class (statement lines 8098-8108, tag 0AZ3). The proof is a careful three-stage reduction: first over the irreducible components, then along a modification after which the module becomes a successive extension of invertible sheaves, and finally to a single effective Cartier divisor, where the computation of the right hand side as a sum of residue weighted lengths is converted into dim_k Gamma(D, O_D) by the pushdown formula. Each stage uses a different additivity statement and none of them is the lemma itself, so the claim is H2.
